leakage_proxy.disclaimer: Near-duplicate grouping uses average hash similarity. It is not equivalent to verified subject IDs.
leakage_proxy.ahash_interpretation: Only 24.6% of identical-aHash pairs share a label, so aHash is too coarse for subject inference on this dataset. Use exact MD5 duplicates as hard evidence; do not equate aHash groups with subject IDs.

filename_analysis.subject_id_evidence: No explicit subject/person ID field was found. Filenames use cluster_<0-7>_<image_id>, where cluster maps 1:1 to blood-group folder. Numeric image_ids are unique across the whole dataset (0..5999 style indexing), so they behave like global sample indices, not verified participant IDs. Near-duplicate aHash grouping is an imperfect proxy and must not be treated as true subjects.

reported_resnet50_accuracy_source.notes: Value comes from saved notebook cell output after model.evaluate(valid_gen). valid_gen is built from the 20% test split, which is also passed as validation_data during fit().

split_strategy.prior_shuffle: data.sample(frac=1) with NO random_state, then reset_index
split_strategy.reason_not_fully_deterministic: Unseeded DataFrame.sample(frac=1) reorders rows before train_test_split. Even with random_state=42, the content mapped to shuffled indices changes across runs.
split_strategy.validation_set: None dedicated; test split used as validation_data during training

resnet50_architecture.folder_name_mismatch: Folder is Resnet34 but code uses ResNet50

leakage_and_evaluation_risks: Random image-level 80/20 split with no subject constraint
No verified subject IDs in filenames or metadata
Test split used as validation during training (no held-out final test)
Unseeded shuffle before split reduces reproducibility of the exact 81.42% figure
Hardcoded label index map in inference cells may disagree with train_gen.class_indices order
Prediction confidence is not a calibrated probability
